templates.title: Clause 4 Context of the organization
templates.description: Implements AIMS-00: Clause 4 Context of the organization - determine the internal and external issues and the organisation's role in each AI activity, record what interested parties require of the AI management system, set the boundary the AIMS covers, and establish the processes the AIMS is made of and how they hand off to each other.

title.en: Determine the organisation's role in each AI activity and the issues that bear on it

description.en: Walk the AI activities the organisation is involved in and settle, for each, whether it builds the system, supplies it to others, deploys one it bought, or only consumes an output. Then record the internal issues - skills, funding, the governance already running, how much risk the business will carry - and the external ones, including the regulation in each market it operates in, sector expectations, and the suppliers its models and data come from. The role is the load-bearing answer: a deployer of a bought model and the builder of that same model carry different obligations, and a role recorded wrongly here makes every later clause answer a question the organisation was never asked. Attach the dated context record.

evidenceHint.en: Dated context record: internal and external issues, with the role held for every AI activity listed against it

text.en: List the AI activities the organisation develops, supplies, deploys or uses.
Decide the role held in each one and record what settled the answer.
Record the internal issues that affect what the AIMS can achieve.
Record the external issues, naming the market or regulator each applies in.
Date the record and name the person who compiled it.

title.en: Catalogue the parties with an interest in the organisation's AI and what each one requires

description.en: Name the parties whose needs bear on the AI management system - customers, the people affected by what the systems decide, regulators and supervisory bodies, employees who operate or are assessed by them, the suppliers of models and data, and any group with a body that speaks for it. Against each, record the requirement actually held rather than a label: 'explainability' tells an implementer nothing, while 'must be able to tell a rejected applicant which factors drove the decision' can be checked. Then mark which of those requirements the organisation adopts as requirements of the AIMS, because the adopted ones are what later clauses have to satisfy, and a party listed with nothing adopted quietly drops out of the system. Attach the interested-party register.

evidenceHint.en: Interested-party register giving each party, the requirement it holds in checkable terms, and whether the management system adopts it

text.en: Name every party whose needs bear on the AI management system.
Write down the requirement each party actually holds, in checkable terms.
Mark which of those requirements the AIMS adopts as its own.
Note the requirements deliberately not adopted and the reason why.
Date the register and record who confirmed each entry.

title.en: Scope the management system to named units, sites and AI activities and justify each exclusion

description.en: Turn the context and party findings into a boundary a reader can test: which legal entities, business units, sites and AI activities sit inside the AIMS, which systems it covers end to end and which only in part, and where it hands off to a supplier, a customer or another management system already running. Anything deliberately left outside is named with the reason it is outside, because an unstated exclusion reads as an oversight to an auditor and as a denial to a customer. Issue it as a dated, versioned document so later clauses cite a boundary that cannot move without a trace. Attach the issued scope statement.

evidenceHint.en: Versioned boundary statement naming every entity, location and AI activity inside it, with a reason recorded against everything left out

text.en: Carry the context and party findings into a boundary draft.
Name every legal entity, site and AI activity that sits inside.
State where the boundary hands off to a supplier or a customer.
Record each exclusion together with the reason it sits outside.
Issue the statement carrying a version number and a date.

title.en: Map the AIMS processes, their owners and the hand-offs between them

description.en: Clause 4.4 asks for the management system itself, not a folder of policies. List the processes the AIMS is made of - how AI risk gets assessed, how a system is approved into use, how concerns and incidents are handled, how competence is kept current, how the system is audited and reviewed - and for each one name its owner, what it takes in, what it produces and which process consumes that output. Record where each process is documented rather than restating it here: this task connects them, it does not perform them. The failure it prevents is a set of processes that each work alone while nothing joins them, so a risk assessment produces a treatment nobody schedules and an audit finding reaches no review. Attach the process map with its owner and hand-off table.

evidenceHint.en: Process map for the management system: every process with its owner, its inputs, its outputs and the process that consumes each output

text.en: List the processes the AI management system is actually made of.
Name an owner for each process and where it is documented.
Record what each process takes in and what it hands on.
Draw the hand-off from every output to the process that uses it.
Flag any process whose output nothing downstream consumes.

title.en: Reconcile the declared scope against the AI activities the organisation is actually running

description.en: Take an independent view of what is actually running - the AI systems in production, the pilots teams have started, the vendors being paid - and compare it with the boundary statement in both directions: an AI activity nobody declared, and a declared activity that no longer exists. Re-read the context record and the interested-party register in the same pass, because a new market, a new supervisory authority or a change of model supplier invalidates them while the documents still look healthy. Record every discrepancy with an owner and what was done about it, and carry the corrections into the statement and the registers rather than leaving them in the review note. Attach the reconciliation record with its discrepancy list.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation record listing every undeclared or retired activity, the context and party entries revised, and the owner of each correction

text.en: Take an independent list of AI systems, pilots and vendors.
Match each running activity to a line in the boundary statement.
Match each scoped activity back to something still running.
Re-read the context and party records for changes since issue.
Record every gap with an owner and the correction made.
Carry the corrections into the statement and registers in the same pass.

templates.title: Clause 5 Leadership
templates.description: Implements AIMS-01: the acts top management performs itself — demonstrating commitment to the AI management system, issuing the AI policy under its own authority, and conferring AIMS roles, responsibilities and authorities on named people who can be held to them.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Top management (accountable executive sponsoring the AIMS)

title.en: Name the top-management holders of AIMS accountability and the decisions reserved to them

description.en: Top management is a role in this standard, not a job title, so write down which named individuals or which body holds it for the AI management system and which AI decisions cannot be taken without them — approving the policy, accepting AI risk above a stated level, releasing a system to users, withdrawing one. Left implicit, the accountability lands on whoever happens to chair the meeting, and an auditor is shown a governance diagram nobody in it has agreed to. Give every holder a deputy, because an unavailable approver is the usual reason a reserved decision quietly gets taken one level down. Attach the statement naming the holders and the decisions they hold.

evidenceHint.en: Accountability statement listing each named top-management holder, their deputy and the AI decisions that cannot proceed without them

text.en: List the AI decisions that must not be taken below top management.
Name the individual or body holding each of those decisions.
Record a deputy for every holder named.
Have each named holder confirm the accountability in writing.
Date the statement and circulate it to the AIMS participants.

title.en: Issue the AI policy under a dated top-management approval

description.en: The policy becomes the organisation's policy at the moment top management puts its name to it, so capture that act: the text as approved, who approved it, the date it takes effect, and the message telling the organisation it applies to them. A policy sitting in a document library with no record of who authorised it is a draft whatever its header says, and the first person asked to follow it against a delivery deadline will treat it as one. Drafting the policy's content, its alignment with other policies and its review cycle belongs to the AI policy framework control; what is recorded here is the issuing decision. Attach the approval record together with the announcement.

evidenceHint.en: Signed and dated approval record for the policy as issued, with the leadership announcement that put it into force

text.en: Fix the policy text that is being approved.
Record the approver, their role and the approval date.
State the date the policy takes effect from.
Send the announcement to everyone the policy binds.
Store the approved text where staff can reach it.

title.en: Authorise each AIMS role holder and record the decisions that holder may take

description.en: Assigning a role is only half of it: the holder also needs conferred authority and written limits on it — what may be approved alone, what must be escalated, what may be stopped. For each holder record the decisions conferred, the limit on them, and the reporting line that carries AIMS performance back to top management. Without the limits the holder either over-reaches or refers everything upward, and the assignment stops being a delegation of authority at all. The detailed role and accountability structures sit with the internal organization control; this is top management conferring the authority. Attach the authorisation record covering every holder.

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation record: one entry per holder giving the decisions held, the limits placed on them and the escalation route

text.en: Take the reserved decisions from the accountability statement.
Assign each decision to a named holder with a limit.
Write down what each holder must escalate upward.
Name who reports AIMS performance to top management.
Have top management sign the authorisations as conferred.

title.en: Minute the leadership decisions that directed, resourced and unblocked the AIMS this period

description.en: Through the period leadership keeps taking decisions that either support the AI management system or quietly starve it — budget and people released to it, an item put on or dropped from an agenda, an escalation settled in favour of a launch date. Record them as they happen, with the date, the decision and who took it, rather than reconstructing a commitment narrative at audit time out of meetings that were about something else. This is the running record of direction and support, separate from the formal management review, which carries its own required inputs and outputs. Attach the dated decision log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Dated log of leadership decisions for the period: AI agenda items, resources released, escalations settled and by whom

text.en: Put AI management system items on the leadership agenda.
Minute each decision with its date and decision-taker.
Record the resources released and to which AIMS activity.
Log every escalation reaching top management and its outcome.
File the minute extracts as they are approved.

title.en: Trace each decision reserved to top management back to the person who actually took it

description.en: Take a sample of the decisions the organisation reserved to top management — a policy change, an AI risk accepted, a system released or withdrawn — and find out who actually took each one. Reserved decisions drift downward silently: an approval given by a delegate, a vacancy that left a holder unnamed for a quarter, a reorganisation that moved the reporting line somewhere below top management, and the governance statement still reads correctly throughout. Record the gaps, who they were raised with and what was corrected, and refresh the authorisation record in the same pass. Attach the review record with its sample and findings.

evidenceHint.en: Review record naming the decisions sampled, the approver found for each, the gaps raised and the corrections made

text.en: Sample decisions taken in the period against the reserved list.
Find the approver of record for each sampled decision.
Flag any taken below the authorised holder.
Check each holder named is still in post.
Correct the authorisation record and report the gaps.

templates.title: AI risk and impact assessment framework
templates.description: Implements AIMS-02A: builds the instrument the organisation judges AI risk with — the criteria and scales, the method by which a risk is identified, analysed and scored, the rules for choosing treatment and signing off what is left over, and the threshold above which an impact assessment becomes mandatory. It produces the method and keeps it calibrated; assessing any particular AI system against it happens under Clause 8.

title.en: Set the AI risk criteria, scales and acceptance thresholds the method will apply

description.en: Before any system is assessed, write down what risk is being measured against: the consequence scale with a concrete example of each band, the likelihood scale and the period it is judged over, the level above which a risk may not simply be accepted, and the point at which an impact assessment on affected individuals becomes mandatory rather than optional. Name, by role, who may accept a risk in each band. Without this every team invents its own high, two assessments of the same system cannot be compared, and a risk ends up accepted by whoever happened to run the assessment. Attach the approved criteria, dated, with the accepting authority shown against each band.

evidenceHint.en: Approved criteria sheet: consequence and likelihood bands with worked examples, the escalation line, and the accepting role for each band

text.en: Write the consequence scale with a worked example for every band.
Write the likelihood scale and state the period it is judged over.
Fix the level above which a risk cannot be accepted without escalation.
State the threshold that makes an impact assessment mandatory.
Name by role who may accept a risk in each band, and get the criteria approved.

title.en: Design the risk assessment method: inputs required, analysis steps and the scoring rule

description.en: Set out the method somebody follows to produce a risk entry: which inputs must be on the table before they start, how risks are identified rather than recalled from memory, how consequence and likelihood combine into one level, where the findings of an impact assessment enter that level, and what is written down at each step. The test of a method is that two competent people given the same system reach the same level; where it leaves that to judgement, the register it fills is not comparable across systems and the ranking it produces cannot be trusted. This task produces the method itself and its version number, not an assessment of any live system.

evidenceHint.en: Issued method document, version-numbered, naming what an assessor must hold before starting, each analysis step, and how a single level is produced

text.en: List the inputs an assessor must hold before starting.
Set out how risks are found rather than recalled from memory.
State how consequence and likelihood combine into one level.
Say where impact findings change the level a risk carries.
Have a colleague who did not write it follow the draft once.
Give the method a version number and an issue date.

title.en: Establish the treatment rules: option choice, Annex A comparison, residual-risk sign-off

description.en: Decide once, in writing, how a scored risk becomes a decision: which treatment options an owner may choose between, what has to sit behind the option chosen, that any set of controls selected is laid against Annex A so a necessary control cannot be quietly omitted, and what the statement of applicability must say for an inclusion and for an exclusion. Name the role that signs off the risk left over after treatment and the record that sign-off lands in. Left to the moment, these calls are made by whoever is in the room, exclusions carry no reason anyone can audit later, and nobody can say who accepted what.

evidenceHint.en: Written treatment procedure giving the available options, the comparison step against Annex A, the statement-of-applicability format, and the approver of leftover risk

text.en: List the treatment options an owner may choose between.
Require the comparison against Annex A before a control set is final.
Fix what the statement of applicability says for an inclusion and an exclusion.
Name the role that signs off leftover risk and where it is recorded.
Walk one past decision through the rules to find where they stay silent.

title.en: Log every case where the criteria or method did not fit, and how each was closed

description.en: Assessors hit the edges of a method constantly: a band that does not fit the harm in front of them, a new kind of system the input list has no question for, a customer or regulator asking something the scales cannot answer, an incident whose severity the consequence scale under-read. Capture each one as it happens, with what was proposed, and close it with either the amendment made or the reason none was needed. Uncaptured, people work around the scale instead of fixing it, the drift is invisible, and the annual review arrives with no evidence of what did not work.

evidenceHint.en: Framework change log for the period: each challenge, who raised it, and the amendment made or the reason none was needed

text.en: Open an entry whenever an assessor says a band does not fit.
Record each new kind of system the input list cannot cover.
Note every outside question the scales could not answer.
Close each entry with the amendment made or why none was needed.

title.en: Evaluate whether the criteria ever forced a different decision, and revise those that did not

description.en: Take the assessments completed under the method in the period and ask what the criteria actually did: how many risks landed in each band, whether anything ever crossed the acceptance line, and whether a treatment decision would have gone differently had the thresholds not been there. A band nothing ever lands in, or a line no risk ever crosses, is not evidence of a safe estate; it is a scale that cannot discriminate, and it will keep passing everything it is pointed at. Record the distribution, name the bands that did no work, carry the revisions into the criteria and the method together, and re-issue both. The subject under review is the instrument, not the systems it was used on.

evidenceHint.en: Calibration review record: the band distribution for the period, the bands found inert, the revisions made, and the re-issued version number

text.en: Count how many risks landed in each band this period.
Find any band no assessment has ever placed a risk in.
Check whether the acceptance line ever blocked a decision.
Revise the bands that did no work and re-issue the criteria.
State the version the next assessments must be run under.

templates.title: AI objectives and planning of AIMS changes
templates.description: Implements AIMS-02B: set AI objectives at the levels that matter, expressed so they can be measured and missed; plan the work, resources and accountability that will reach them; and put every change to the AI management system itself through a planned route, so its purpose, consequences and reallocated responsibilities are decided before it takes effect rather than reconstructed afterwards.

title.en: Express each AI policy commitment as a measurable objective with an owner and a date

description.en: Take the AI policy commitment by commitment and turn each one into an objective somebody can be measured against: a named measure, a target value, a due date and the function that owns it. An objective phrased as an intention — use AI responsibly, improve model quality — cannot be missed, so it never shows as behind and never triggers anything. Include the objectives implied by the risk and impact treatment decisions already taken, because a treatment nobody carries an objective for is the one that quietly does not happen. Attach the objectives register as it stands once the set is agreed.

evidenceHint.en: Agreed AI objectives register, one row per objective giving its measure, target value, due date and the accountable function

text.en: List the commitments the published AI policy actually makes.
Take the risk and impact treatment decisions that need an objective.
State each objective as a measure, a target value and a due date.
Rewrite any objective that nobody could ever show as missed.
Name the function accountable for moving each measure.

title.en: Build an achievement plan for every AI objective, naming resources, owner and due date

description.en: For each objective in the register, set out the plan that actually gets there: the work to be done, the resources it consumes, the single person accountable, the date it completes and how the result will be judged when it does. Objectives without plans are the common failure at this clause — the register reads healthy all year while the work was never resourced, and the gap only surfaces at the deadline. Where a plan depends on budget or people that are not yet committed, say so in the plan rather than assuming them. Attach the plans alongside the register.

evidenceHint.en: Per-objective delivery plans covering the work, the committed resources, the accountable person, the completion date and how each result is judged

text.en: Break each objective into the work that will deliver it.
Name the people, budget and tooling every plan depends on.
Give each plan one accountable owner and a completion date.
State how the result will be evaluated when the plan closes.
Confirm the named resources are committed rather than assumed.
Set the cadence at which progress against the plan is reported.

title.en: Set the route a change to the AI management system must travel before it takes effect

description.en: Write down how a change to the management system itself is proposed, weighed and approved: who may raise one, what must be stated about its purpose and its likely consequences, who decides, and how responsibilities and resources are reallocated when it lands. Changes made outside a route arrive as surprises — a scope narrowed here, an owner reassigned there — and every arrangement that referenced the old shape quietly stops matching. Keep this to the management system: operational and product changes are controlled elsewhere. Attach the written route once it is approved.

evidenceHint.en: Approved change-planning procedure for the AIMS, naming what must be stated in a proposal, the approval point, and the consistency and resource checks applied

text.en: List what counts as a change to the management system itself.
Require a stated purpose and expected effect for each proposal.
Add a check that the change leaves the AIMS internally consistent.
Name who approves a change and who reallocates responsibilities.
Require resources to be confirmed before a change is approved.

title.en: Minute every AIMS change made in the period with its purpose, effects and approval

description.en: Each time the management system changes — its scope, roles, processes or documented arrangements — open a record stating why the change was made, what effect was expected, what else it touched, which resources and responsibilities moved, and who approved it and from when. Without that record a reviewer cannot separate a planned change from drift, and the organisation keeps no evidence that consequences were weighed before the change rather than discovered after it. Changes that bypassed the route still get a record, marked as unplanned. Attach the period's change records.

evidenceHint.en: Dated AIMS change log for the period, each entry giving the reason, the expected and knock-on effects, the resources and responsibilities moved, the approver and the effective date

text.en: Open a record for every proposed change to the AIMS.
Capture the purpose, the expected effect and the side effects weighed.
Record the resources released and the responsibilities moved.
Note the approval decision, the approver and the effective date.
Add changes that were made without planning, marked as unplanned.

title.en: Reassess the objective set at period end and confirm each change landed as planned

description.en: Close the register row by row: met, missed, revised or retired, with the final measure set against the target the plan committed to. Then check that each change to the management system produced the effect its record predicted, because a change planned carefully and landed differently leaves the system describing arrangements nobody works to. Carry what is still open into the next period's objectives rather than reissuing last year's list unchanged, and record who approved the revised set. Attach the review record together with the approved objectives for the coming period.

evidenceHint.en: Period-end review record giving the outcome and final measure for each objective, the post-change verification notes, and the approved objective set for the next period

text.en: Close each objective as met, missed, revised or retired.
Compare the final measure with the target the plan committed to.
Check each AIMS change delivered the effect its record predicted.
Re-derive the next period's objectives from the current policy.
Record who approved the revised objective set and when.

templates.title: Clause 7 Support
templates.description: Implements AIMS-03: determine and provide the resources the AI management system needs, make the people whose work affects AI performance competent and aware of the AI policy, settle the internal and external communications the AIMS depends on, and control the documented information it creates and relies on.

title.en: Determine the people, compute, data access and budget the AI management system needs to run

description.en: Work through what establishing, running and improving the AIMS actually consumes — the people who staff the governance, assessment and monitoring work, the tooling and compute those activities depend on, the access to systems and data that reviewers need, and the money that pays for it — then set each need against what the organisation holds today. Where a shortfall is real, record the decision taken on it, including a decision not to fund it, because an unfunded requirement that nobody wrote down resurfaces later as an unexplained gap in whichever clause depended on it. Attach the resourcing record with the date it was agreed.

evidenceHint.en: Dated resourcing record setting each AIMS activity against the staffing, tooling and funding provided, with the decision taken on every shortfall

text.en: List the work the AIMS itself requires each year, activity by activity.
Name the roles, tooling and compute each of those activities consumes.
Compare each need against the staffing and budget available now.
Record the funding decision taken on every gap, refusals included.

title.en: Map each role whose work affects AI system performance to the competence it must hold

description.en: Start from the roles that actually change AI outcomes — the people who build and evaluate models, the ones who approve a deployment, the reviewers who sign off assessments, the operators watching systems in production — and state, per role, what somebody must know or have done to hold it. Then assess the current holders against that statement and agree the action that closes each shortfall, with an owner and a date. A competence claim resting on a job title is not a claim anybody can check: what makes this defensible is that the qualification, course record or documented experience behind each entry is retained and can be produced on request. Attach the matrix together with the index of those records.

evidenceHint.en: Competence matrix per role with current holders assessed against it, the agreed closing actions, and an index of the qualification and training records retained

text.en: Select the roles whose work changes how an AI system performs.
State the knowledge, training or experience each of those roles needs.
Assess the current holders against the statement for their role.
Agree a training, hiring or mentoring action for every shortfall found.
File the certificates and records that evidence each competence claim.

title.en: Schedule the internal and external AI communications, naming what is said, to whom and by which route

description.en: Decide, for every thing the AIMS has to say, who says it, who receives it, what makes it go out, and over which channel. Internally that covers policy changes, objectives, assessment outcomes and incidents reaching the teams and the governance forum; externally it covers what regulators, customers, suppliers and other interested parties are told about how the organisation governs its AI, and who is authorised to say it. Name one approver for external statements, because the failure this prevents is two parts of the organisation describing the same governance position differently in public and neither knowing the other spoke. Attach the communication plan.

evidenceHint.en: Communication plan carrying one row per message: subject, audience, trigger or frequency, channel, and the named sender or approver

text.en: List what the AIMS must communicate internally and externally.
Name the audience and the sender for each of those messages.
Set the trigger or frequency that makes each message go out.
Choose the channel each audience actually reads.
Route every external AI statement through one named approver.

title.en: Log every AIMS document issued, revised, superseded or withdrawn in the period, with its approver and version

description.en: Keep one row per movement of AIMS documented information: the document, its version, who approved it and on what date, where it is held, who it went to, and — where it was replaced or withdrawn — what became of the copy people had been using. Include documents of external origin the AIMS depends on, such as a standard, a regulator's guidance or a supplier's model documentation, because an obsolete external document still in circulation misleads exactly as an obsolete internal one does and nothing else is tracking it. A superseded version left reachable beside its replacement is the condition these rows exist to make visible. Attach the register export for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Documented-information register export covering the period, showing each version approved, distributed, replaced or destroyed and where the copies now sit

text.en: Record each new or revised AIMS document with its approver and date.
Mark the superseded version and remove it from circulation.
Check the storage location and access list stated for each document.
Add the external-origin documents the AIMS relies on to the register.
Apply the retention or disposal rule due on documents this period.

title.en: Sample people doing work under the organisation's control and test what they know of the AI policy

description.en: Awareness is claimed by an attendance list and disproved by a conversation, so draw a sample across the roles the AIMS reaches — contractors and recent joiners included, since they are the likeliest gap — and ask each person three things: what the AI policy asks of their own work, how what they do contributes to the AIMS working, and what follows if they depart from it. Write the answers down as given rather than as a pass mark, note which version of the briefing each person had actually received, and carry the weak areas into the next round of briefing rather than closing the task on the sample alone. Attach the sample test with its findings.

evidenceHint.en: Awareness sample test naming who was asked, what each could state about the policy, their contribution and the consequences, and the briefing gaps it exposed

text.en: Draw a sample spanning employees, contractors and recent joiners.
Ask each person what the AI policy requires of their own work.
Ask what their role contributes and what nonconformity would cause.
Note the briefing version each person in the sample had received.
Feed every weak answer into the next awareness briefing.

templates.title: Clause 8 Operation
templates.description: Implements AIMS-04: plan and control the processes that operate the organisation's AI systems, and actually perform the AI risk assessment, the risk treatment and the AI system impact assessment on schedule and when a change triggers one, keeping the record each produces.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: AI Governance Lead / AI System Owner

title.en: Schedule the risk and impact assessments each AI system owes and the events that trigger an early one

description.en: The framework says how an assessment is performed; this says when, against which system, and who runs it. Give every AI system the AIMS covers a due date for its risk assessment and a due date for its impact assessment, then write the events that pull those dates forward: a retrained or replaced model, a new deployment context, a new user population, a new data source, a change of provider. A schedule carrying no trigger list only ever fires on the anniversary, so a system that changed in March is still assessed against the shape it had in December. Attach the dated schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Dated assessment schedule: one row per AI system giving both due dates, the person accountable for running it, and the events that bring an assessment forward

text.en: List every AI system the AIMS covers and the release now running.
Set the next due date for each system's risk assessment.
Set the next due date for each system's impact assessment.
Write the change events that force an assessment to re-run early.
Name the person accountable for running each scheduled assessment.

title.en: Turn the actions planned under clause 6.1 into operating controls inside each AI process

description.en: Planning produced a list of actions to address AI risks and opportunities; until each exists as a step somebody performs, it is still a list. Take the actions that apply to a given AI system and place each one inside the process that operates it - a pre-deployment check somebody signs, a threshold the monitoring enforces, an approval the deployment step cannot skip - naming who performs it and what it leaves behind. Say which steps run inside the organisation and which run at a provider, because an operating plan that stops at the organisation's boundary leaves the outsourced half of the process uncontrolled. Attach the process description with the control points marked.

evidenceHint.en: Process description per AI system with the control points marked, the performer named against each, and the externally provided steps identified

text.en: List the clause 6.1 actions that apply to this AI system.
Place each action as a step in the process that operates it.
Name who performs each control point and at what moment.
Mark the steps performed by an external provider rather than in-house.
Record what each control point produces as its output.

title.en: Complete each action on the AI risk treatment plan and show what it changed in operation

description.en: Work the treatment plan line by line: for every action record that it was done, the date it took effect, and the observable difference in how the AI system now runs - a filter now applied, a human review now required, a data source now withdrawn. An action closed with a date but no observable change is the one that reappears at the next assessment with the same risk still attached to it. Where an action cannot be delivered as planned, record what was done instead and refer it back to the people who own the treatment approach, rather than editing the plan to match what happened. Attach the worked plan with the evidence for each action.

evidenceHint.en: Worked treatment plan showing, per action, the delivery date, the evidence attached and the change observed in the running system

text.en: Take the plan's treatment actions in their planned order.
Deliver each action and record the date it took effect.
Capture the observable change each action made in operation.
Mark any action that could not be delivered as planned.
Attach the evidence produced by each completed action.

title.en: Run every assessment that falls due or is triggered in the period and file its record

description.en: Work the schedule: for each AI system whose risk assessment or impact assessment has come due, or whose trigger has fired, perform it by the established method and file the result against that system with the date, the version assessed, who took part and the outcome reached. The impact half asks what the system does to the people and groups exposed to it, so it is worked with Legal/DPO present rather than by the system owner alone. An assessment performed and never filed is indistinguishable, a year later, from one never performed. Where a trigger fired and no assessment followed, file that reason in the same place so the gap is visible rather than absent.

evidenceHint.en: Assessment records filed for the period, one per AI system and version, naming date, participants and outcome, with the reasons logged where a triggered run did not happen

text.en: Select the systems whose assessment comes due this period.
Add any system whose change trigger fired since the last run.
Perform the risk assessment by the established method.
Perform the impact assessment on the people and groups affected.
File each result against the system version that was assessed.
Record the reason where a triggered assessment did not run.

title.en: Reconcile the assessments performed against the ones owed and re-check that each treatment still holds

description.en: Put the schedule and the filed records side by side and name every row carrying no record, every record answering no row, and every trigger that fired without an assessment following it. Then sample the treatment actions completed earlier in the period and check they are still operating as described, because an action delivered in January and quietly reverted in April leaves a plan that still reads as complete. Record each gap with the reason it opened, hand the ones needing correction to the improvement process rather than closing them here, and carry the systems whose risk has moved into the next schedule instead of leaving them for the anniversary. Attach the reconciliation.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation record listing each scheduled assessment against its filed evidence, the triggers left unanswered, and the sampled treatments with the cause of every gap found

text.en: Match each scheduled assessment to the record filed for it.
List the triggers that fired with no assessment following.
Sample completed treatment actions and check they still run.
Note where the assessed risk has moved since the last cycle.
Hand any gap needing correction to the improvement process.

templates.title: AIMS monitoring, measurement and evaluation
templates.description: Implements AIMS-05A: run the AIMS measurement programme required by clause 9.1. Decide which AIMS processes, controls and AI system properties are measured, fix the method, data source and target behind each measure, set when readings are taken and separately when they are analysed, take them on schedule, and evaluate what the resulting numbers say about the AIMS performing and being effective.

title.en: Select the AIMS processes, controls and AI system properties that will be measured

description.en: Decide what the organisation will actually put a number against: the AIMS processes whose performance matters, the controls whose operation has to stay visible between audits, and the properties of the AI systems the AIMS claims to hold in check. Take the AI objectives as an input rather than restating them - the objectives say where the organisation intends to get to, this list says which of those movements can be observed at all. Without it the measurement programme quietly becomes whatever data was easiest to export, and everything awkward to export goes unwatched. Attach the scope list with the reason each item was chosen.

evidenceHint.en: Measurement scope list naming every AIMS process, control and AI system property chosen, with the reason each was selected

text.en: List the AIMS processes whose performance the organisation relies on.
Add the controls whose operation has to stay visible between audits.
Add the AI system properties the AIMS claims to hold in check.
Record against each item why it was judged worth measuring.
Mark the items that matter but cannot currently be observed.

title.en: Set the method, data source and target for every AIMS measure

description.en: Turn each selected item into a measure somebody else could reproduce: the exact calculation, the system the numbers are read from, who reads them, and the target or threshold that decides whether a result is acceptable. A measure named without a method produces a different number every time the person producing it changes, which is precisely the invalid result clause 9.1 asks the organisation to design out. Where a measure is a count, say what is counted and what is excluded; where it is a rate, name both the numerator and the denominator. Attach the measure definitions.

evidenceHint.en: Measure definition sheet giving, per indicator, its calculation, the system it is read from, the reader and the acceptance threshold

text.en: Write the calculation for each measure so two people get one answer.
Name the system or record the numbers are extracted from.
State the numerator and denominator for every rate or ratio.
Set the target, threshold or tolerance the result is judged against.
Name the person accountable for producing each measure.

title.en: Schedule when each measure is taken and when its results are analysed

description.en: Clause 9.1 separates two timings that organisations routinely collapse into one: when a reading is taken, and when somebody sits down and works out what the readings mean. Fix both for every measure, because a weekly reading nobody analyses until the annual review is a year of data that changed no decision. Name who performs the analysis and where its output goes, so the numbers arrive at a decision rather than at a dashboard. Attach the measurement calendar covering every measure on the scope list.

evidenceHint.en: Measurement calendar showing each indicator's reading interval, its separate analysis point, and who performs each

text.en: Set the reading interval for each measure on the scope list.
Set the separate date or cadence at which results get analysed.
Name who performs the analysis and who receives the output.
Check no measure has a reading cadence without an analysis point.

title.en: Capture each scheduled reading and state what it says about AIMS performance

description.en: On every scheduled date, take the reading by the defined method, compare it against its target, and write the short judgement that travels with it - inside tolerance, drifting, or breached and why. A stored number carrying no interpretation forces whoever opens it months later to reconstruct the meaning from memory, and a reading that was never taken has to show as missed rather than as a gap the eye slides over. Where a result crosses its threshold, note what was raised and where it was routed, without carrying out that work here. Attach the dated results for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Dated results set for the period: every reading taken, its comparison against threshold, the judgement written against it, and any missed reading marked as such

text.en: Take each reading on its scheduled date by the defined method.
Compare every result against its target or tolerance band.
Write the one-line judgement that accompanies each result.
Mark any reading that was missed, with the reason it was missed.
Note where a breached threshold was routed for action.

title.en: Evaluate whether the measure set still shows AIMS effectiveness, and revise it

description.en: Take the period's results as a body and ask what they demonstrate about the AIMS performing and being effective, rather than whether each number was collected on time. Two failures hide at this level: an indicator that has read green every period since the day it was created and therefore discriminates nothing, and a part of the AIMS that changed without any measure following it. Decide for each indicator whether it is kept, retired or replaced, and carry the survivors and the additions back into the scope list and the calendar in the same pass, so the evidence the audit programme and the management review draw on is current. Attach the evaluation record with reviewer and date.

evidenceHint.en: Periodic evaluation record marking each indicator kept, retired or replaced, with the conclusion drawn about AIMS performance, plus reviewer and date

text.en: Read the period's results together and state what they demonstrate.
Flag every measure that has never varied and decide its fate.
Check whether any changed part of the AIMS now has no measure.
Mark each indicator as kept, retired or replaced with a reason.
Carry the revisions into the scope list and the calendar.

templates.title: AIMS internal audit programme
templates.description: Implements AIMS-05B: runs a planned programme of internal AIMS audits — a schedule built from process importance and earlier findings, auditors chosen for competence and held clear of the work they own, stated criteria and coverage for each audit, and findings reported to the managers accountable for what was audited.
templates.defaultOwnerHint: Internal Audit Lead / AI Governance Lead

title.en: Schedule every AIMS process into the audit programme by importance and prior findings

description.en: Lay out which parts of the AI management system are audited when across the cycle, and let the spacing carry a reason: a process that produced nonconformities last time, changed materially, or carries the organisation's highest-risk AI systems is audited more often than a stable one. Record the method each audit will use and who is accountable for it happening. Without a written programme, audits drift towards the areas that are easy to book and the untouched ones surface first at a certification visit. Attach the programme with its approval date.

evidenceHint.en: Approved programme for the cycle listing each planned audit, its month, its method, the accountable owner and the risk reasoning behind its frequency

text.en: List every AIMS process, clause and AI system inside the audited scope.
Rate each entry by risk and by nonconformities raised in earlier cycles.
Place each audit in a month and state the method it will use.
Name the person accountable for each planned audit going ahead.
Obtain approval of the programme and date it before the cycle opens.

title.en: Define the criteria, scope and exclusions of an audit before fieldwork opens

description.en: Before any fieldwork starts, put in writing the criteria the audit works to — the AIMS policies, procedures, objectives and obligations that conformity is measured against — and which processes, sites and AI systems sit inside its boundary. Name what is left out as plainly as what is taken in, and give the reason for leaving it, because a process nobody looked at is otherwise read afterwards as a process looked at and found sound. Get the terms agreed by the person who owns the programme, and attach the agreed terms of reference.

evidenceHint.en: Agreed terms of reference per audit, naming the criteria applied, the processes and AI systems inside the boundary, and every omission with the reason for it

text.en: List the AIMS policies, procedures and objectives the audit measures conformity against.
Name the processes, sites and AI systems that sit inside the boundary.
Write down every process or system left out, and the reason for leaving it.
Have the programme owner and the process owner agree the boundary in writing.
Hand the agreed terms of reference to the auditor before any fieldwork starts.

title.en: Select auditors on competence and bar each one from the work they own

description.en: Choose who audits what, and hold two decisions per auditor rather than one: what makes them competent here — audit method, AIMS knowledge, enough grasp of AI systems to test the claim in front of them — and what they are barred from because they built, run or manage it. Impartiality is the part that quietly fails in a small organisation, where the only person who understands the model pipeline is the person who owns it; where that happens, record the compensating arrangement — an auditor from another function, a swap with a sister site, or an external auditor — rather than letting an owner examine their own work.

evidenceHint.en: Auditor roster giving each person's competence evidence, the areas they may not audit, and the arrangement covering any area with no impartial candidate

text.en: Record the competence evidence held for each proposed auditor.
Map each auditor to the processes they build, run or manage.
Bar every auditor from the areas that mapping returned.
Arrange an external or swapped auditor where no impartial one exists.
Have the programme owner sign off the final auditor assignments.

title.en: Conduct each planned audit and issue its findings to the managers accountable

description.en: Run the audit against its stated criteria: sample real records rather than asking whether a procedure exists, note what was examined so a reader can tell coverage from assertion, and grade what comes back as conformity, nonconformity or an observation that is not yet either. Report the result to the manager accountable for the audited process, with a date on the handover — a finding that lands nowhere in particular has not been reported — and pass nonconformities into the corrective-action route rather than closing them inside the audit.

evidenceHint.en: Audit reports for the cycle showing the records sampled, each finding graded, and a dated distribution list recording which manager received what

text.en: Sample records and interview the people who do the work.
Note every item examined against the criterion it tests.
Grade each finding as conformity, nonconformity or observation.
Send the report to the accountable manager and date the handover.
Route each nonconformity into the corrective-action process.

title.en: Compare the audits delivered against the programme and account for each one missed

description.en: At the end of the cycle read the programme against what actually happened: audits deferred or dropped and the reason, areas that have now gone a full cycle unaudited, and any audit where a reorganisation moved a boundary until the assigned auditor was examining their own work. Look as well for the same finding recurring across audits, because a repeat says the corrective action taken elsewhere did not hold. Carry the answers into the next programme instead of leaving them as observations.

evidenceHint.en: Cycle coverage comparison: planned versus completed audits, deferrals with reasons, areas left unaudited, impartiality lapses found and the revisions made for the next cycle

text.en: Match each planned audit against the report it produced.
List deferred audits with the reason and the new date.
Identify scope areas left unaudited for a full cycle.
Check that no auditor ended up auditing their own area.
Flag findings that recur across audits in the cycle.
Revise the next programme from what this comparison showed.

templates.title: AIMS management review
templates.description: Implements AIMS-05C: hold management reviews of the AIMS at planned intervals with top management present, put the full set of inputs the clause requires in front of them, and carry each sitting out as recorded decisions, actions and resource commitments.

title.en: Schedule the review cycle and name the top managers whose presence makes a sitting valid

description.en: A review that slips a year, or that goes ahead with whoever was free, produces opinions rather than decisions that bind the AIMS. Fix the interval between sittings and put the dates in the calendar, then name by role the senior people whose authority actually covers AIMS change and resourcing, plus the chair and the person who minutes it. State the quorum below which the sitting is postponed rather than held, so a thin meeting fails visibly instead of being written up as a review. Attach the schedule showing the dates, the named roles and the quorum rule.

evidenceHint.en: Review calendar with the named attendee roles, the chair, and the quorum rule that makes a sitting count

text.en: Fix the interval between sittings and put the dates in the calendar.
Name each senior role whose attendance the review requires.
Name the chair and the person who writes the minutes.
State the quorum below which a sitting is postponed.
Confirm each named attendee has accepted the standing invitation.

title.en: Agree the standing input pack a sitting must receive before it can open

description.en: The clause fixes what a review has to consider, so a meeting that discusses whatever the chair had to hand will quietly drop two or three of them and cannot show otherwise afterwards. Build one agenda template that lists every required input - the status of actions from earlier sittings, shifts in the internal and external issues bearing on the AIMS, AIMS performance including nonconformities, the measurement results and the audit findings the performance-evaluation controls already produce, how far the AI objectives were met, feedback from interested parties, and improvement opportunities - and name against each one the person who supplies it and the date it is due. Attach the template with both fields filled for every input.

evidenceHint.en: Agenda template listing each required input with its named supplier and the date it is due to the chair

text.en: List every input the clause requires a review to consider.
Name the person who supplies each input to the chair.
Set a submission date for each input ahead of the sitting.
Point each input at the report that already produces it.
Circulate the completed pack to attendees before the meeting.

title.en: Record what each sitting was told, what it decided and what it changed

description.en: Without a written record made while the discussion is fresh, a sitting's conclusions survive only as recollection: months later nobody can say which option top management picked, what evidence sat in front of them, or which concerns were parked rather than settled. The minutes are what turn a conversation into work the organisation has committed to.

evidenceHint.en: The signed minute book for the period, one entry per sitting

text.en: Take the minutes as the sitting runs, noting who attended and who gave apologies.
Set down, for each item tabled, the discussion held and the conclusion reached.
Write each decision as its own numbered minute, with the reasoning that led to it.
Raise every agreed action in the tracker before the sitting closes, quoting its minute number.
Have the chair approve the draft, then file it with the papers the sitting received.

title.en: Track the actions a sitting raised through to closure before the next one opens

description.en: The status of actions from earlier reviews is itself a required input, so an action list nobody maintains empties the first item on the next agenda and lets a commitment made by top management expire unnoticed. Hold every action from the minutes in one register with its owner, due date, current state and the evidence that justified closing it, chase the owners ahead of the pack deadline, and put anything overdue in front of the chair instead of rolling it forward silently. Attach the register as it stood when the next pack was circulated.

evidenceHint.en: Action register per item raised, carrying owner, due date, state and the proof accepted at closure

text.en: Open a register entry for each action the minutes raised.
Ask each owner for a status update before the pack deadline.
Attach the evidence that justifies closing an action.
Escalate any action past its due date to the review chair.
Carry open items into the next agenda as the first item.

title.en: Verify the period's sittings against the input list, the quorum rule and the decisions they owed

description.en: A review can run on schedule and still fail the clause, by sitting without the named seniors, by never being given two of the required inputs, or by closing items with observations that commit nobody. Once a year read the minutes of every sitting back against the standing input list and the attendance rule, mark each required input no sitting received, each sitting held under quorum, and each agenda item closed with no action attached, then agree with the chair what changes in the next cycle. Attach the check with a finding line per gap.

evidenceHint.en: Annual conformity check over the sittings held, naming each missed input, thin sitting and undecided item

text.en: Read each sitting's minutes against the standing input list.
Mark every required input that no sitting was given.
List sittings that went ahead without meeting quorum.
Flag agenda items closed without an action attached.
Agree with the chair what changes in the next cycle.

templates.title: Clause 10 Improvement
templates.description: Implements AIMS-06: Clause 10 Improvement — routes every AIMS nonconformity from wherever it is raised through containment, cause analysis and a corrective action sized to that cause, drives improvement opportunities to a dated closure that changed something, and re-checks later that each correction actually held.

title.en: Consolidate every route that raises an AIMS nonconformity into one register

description.en: Nonconformities arrive from internal audit findings, breached monitoring thresholds, AI system incidents, complaints from users or affected third parties, supplier failures and the outputs of the management review, and each route tends to keep its own list — so the same weakness is corrected three times and counted as none. Pull the routes into a single register, and write beside it the test that separates a nonconformity (a requirement of the AIMS was not met) from an improvement opportunity (it was met, and could work better), because the two are handled differently and every later task reads this register. Attach the register with its intake routes listed and the open items from the last period loaded into it.

evidenceHint.en: Improvement and nonconformity register, listing the intake routes feeding it and how each open item was classified

text.en: List the routes that raise findings today: audit, monitoring, incident, complaint, supplier and review.
Write the test that separates a nonconformity from an improvement opportunity.
Open a single register and load each route's outstanding items into it.
Agree with every route owner that their findings land here and nowhere else.

title.en: Set the containment steps that run before any cause analysis begins

description.en: A raised nonconformity runs two clocks: what the AI system or process is doing wrong right now, and why it is. This task covers only the first — controlling and correcting the nonconformity itself, and dealing with the consequences it has already produced, such as decisions taken on a faulty model output, data written where it should not have been, or wrong information given to a user. State who may authorise a pause, a rollback or a fallback to human handling, and how affected parties are told, because teams otherwise open a cause investigation while the harm keeps accruing. Attach the containment procedure with the authority levels it names.

evidenceHint.en: Containment procedure naming who may pause or roll back an AI system and how harm already caused is put right

text.en: Name who may pause, roll back or fall back to human handling.
Describe how consequences already produced are found and put right.
Agree per severity how quickly containment is expected to start.
Record the containment taken against the register entry it belongs to.

title.en: Analyse each nonconformity to its cause and test whether it sits elsewhere

description.en: Correcting what was seen leaves the mechanism that produced it intact, so this is where an entry stops being a symptom. Work each nonconformity back to what allowed it — a missing check in the life cycle, a dataset nobody owned, an objective never turned into a measure, a role assigned to a vacant post — and record the cause in those terms rather than as human error, which names nobody's mechanism and can never be eliminated. Then ask the question that decides scope: does the same cause exist in another AI system, dataset or process that simply has not failed yet? Add whatever that finds to the register. The AIMS owner reviews each analysis before a corrective action is sized against it.

evidenceHint.en: Cause analyses for the period, each recording the mechanism that allowed the failure and the other systems checked against it

text.en: Work each entry back from its symptom to the mechanism that permitted it.
Reject any cause stated as individual error with no systemic explanation.
Check the named cause against other AI systems, datasets and processes.
Add further occurrences found by that check to the register as entries.
Decide whether corrective action is warranted, and record the reasoning.

title.en: Close each nonconformity and improvement entry only when something in the AIMS changed

description.en: This is the recurring act the clause produces its evidence from. For every open entry, carry the action agreed against its cause, the owner, what changed in the AIMS as a result — a revised procedure, a new control, an altered objective, a retrained model, a withdrawn use — and the date it closed. Improvement opportunities travel the same path, which is what makes continual improvement of the AIMS visible as worked items rather than an intention stated in a policy. An entry closing with nothing changed is either not a nonconformity or not finished, and the log has to show which. Attach the log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Period log of entries worked and shut, giving the owner, the action taken, the resulting change to the management system and its date

text.en: Record the agreed action against the cause it is meant to eliminate.
Assign an owner and a target date to every open entry in the register.
Capture what changed in the AIMS once the action was carried out.
Close an entry only where that change is evidenced, not merely reported.
Carry open entries forward so none ages quietly out of the register.

title.en: Re-verify closed corrective actions to confirm the cause has not returned

description.en: A corrective action is not proven by somebody having ticked it closed. Sample the entries closed since the previous cycle, weighted towards those whose cause was systemic or whose similar-case check found further occurrences, and look for evidence the cause has actually gone: re-run the monitoring signal that first flagged it, the audit test that failed, or the user reports that prompted it. Where the nonconformity has recurred or the change was quietly reversed, reopen the original entry instead of raising a fresh one, so the recurrence stays attached to its cause and the repeat is visible. Record which closures held and which did not, and pass anything still unresolved to the next management review rather than settling it here.

evidenceHint.en: Effectiveness re-check of sampled closures naming what was tested, which held, which recurred, and the entries reopened

text.en: Sample the entries closed since the previous review cycle.
Re-run the test or signal that originally exposed the nonconformity.
Reopen any entry whose cause returned rather than raising a new one.
Summarise which closures held and which did not, with the reasons.
Hand unresolved or systemic findings to the next management review.

templates.title: A.2 Policies related to AI
templates.description: Implements AIMS-07: keep the written AI policy framework as a maintained set of documents — the topics it covers, the pointers that keep it consistent with the organisation's other policies, and the interval reviews that keep every document current.

title.en: Map the AI policy topics against the documents that already carry them

description.en: Before a word of new policy is written, settle what the framework has to consist of: list the subjects the organisation's AI policy must speak to — acceptable use of AI, data used for training and prompting, model development, human oversight, procurement of AI services — and beside each one name the document that states it today. Several will already sit inside a security, privacy, HR or procurement policy, and copying them into a fresh AI policy creates two statements of the same rule that drift apart at the first amendment. Mark every topic as covered elsewhere, covered but stale, or not covered at all. Attach the dated map.

evidenceHint.en: Dated coverage map pairing each AI subject with the document stating it today, and the uncovered subjects found

text.en: List the AI subjects the framework has to speak to.
Trace each subject to the document that states it today.
Mark the subjects no current document covers at all.
Flag statements that are stale or contradict each other.
Date the map and hold it as the framework's starting point.

title.en: Assemble the AI policy framework with an owner, version and issue date on every document

description.en: Turn the topic map into the framework itself — a single AI policy or a named set of documents — and stamp each document with its owner, version number, issue date and the topics it governs, so a reader can tell which document answers a question and whether the copy in front of them is the current one. Cite the approval that already exists rather than seeking a fresh one here. Where an existing policy already governs a topic well, point to it from the framework's contents page instead of restating the rule, because a restated rule is the one that later contradicts its original. Attach the framework as issued.

evidenceHint.en: The issued AI policy set with a contents page, each document showing its version, date of issue, topics governed and named owner

text.en: Draft or adopt a document for each uncovered topic.
Stamp owner, version and issue date onto each document.
Point to the existing policy wherever one already governs a topic.
Publish the set behind a contents page naming every document.
Cite the approval record that authorised the issued text.

title.en: Reconcile each AI policy statement against the security, privacy and procurement policies it touches

description.en: Read the AI policy clause by clause beside the policies it overlaps and find the places where they say different things: an AI policy permitting customer records in model training while the privacy policy forbids secondary use, a supplier rule that contradicts the procurement standard, an oversight requirement no security policy supports. Record every conflict as a pair of clause references, decide which document is the one that states the rule, and amend the other in the same pass — leaving both texts standing means whichever a team reads first becomes the organisation's position. Attach the reconciliation and the re-issued documents.

evidenceHint.en: Cross-policy reconciliation table giving each conflicting clause pair, the document amended, who decided and the versions re-issued

text.en: List every other policy the AI policy overlaps with.
Read the overlapping clauses side by side for conflicts.
Record each contradiction as a pair of clause references.
Decide which document states the rule and amend the other.
Re-issue both documents under their new version numbers.

title.en: Log every amendment to a framework document with the trigger that prompted it

description.en: Changes reach the framework between scheduled reviews — a new regulation, a class of AI system nobody had deployed before, an incident, a supplier arrangement — and each one needs an entry recording what prompted it, which clauses moved, the version it produced, and which neighbouring policies were re-checked for consistency afterwards. Without the trigger written down, the next reviewer cannot tell a change that was considered and rejected from one that never reached the document at all, and the framework's currency becomes a matter of memory. Attach the log covering the period.

evidenceHint.en: Version history for the period: one entry per change giving its prompt, the clauses touched, the version produced and the consistency re-check

text.en: Open an entry whenever a framework document changes.
Record what prompted the change and who raised it.
Name the clauses amended and the version they produced.
Re-check the neighbouring policies the amended clause touches.
Export the log at the close of the reporting period.

title.en: Hold the interval review of each framework document and record an outcome for every one

description.en: At the planned interval take the documents one at a time and decide in writing whether each stands, needs amendment, or should be withdrawn, because a framework reviewed as a single item lets an untouched sub-document ride on the currency of the one that was actually read. Test each decision against what changed in the period: AI systems newly deployed, regulation that came into force, incidents raised, findings from audits. Record reviewer, date, decision and next due date per document, and carry the amendments through in the same pass rather than logging them as intentions. Attach the review record.

evidenceHint.en: Interval review record listing every document with its reviewer, date, decision, the amendments made and when it falls due again

text.en: Schedule the review at the interval the framework states.
Take each document and decide whether it still stands.
Test each decision against the period's changes and findings.
Amend or withdraw the documents the review rejected.
Record reviewer, date, outcome and the next due date.

templates.title: A.3 Internal organization
templates.description: Implements AIMS-08: A.3 Internal organization — sets out which function is accountable for each decision an AI system passes through, keeps the function that clears a system for use apart from the one that builds it, and runs an internal route by which anyone can raise a concern about an AI system and have it triaged, answered and recorded.

title.en: Map each AI lifecycle decision to the function accountable for it

description.en: Work along the path an AI system takes — proposal, data selection, build, sign-off for use, monitoring, change, retirement — and record which function holds the decision at each point, who deputises when that function is unavailable, and where the decision escalates when it cannot be settled. Name functions rather than individuals, because a map keyed to people is stale the week someone leaves. The output that matters is the set of decision points no function claims: those are the ones taken by whoever happens to be in the room. Attach the map.

evidenceHint.en: Accountability map giving, per decision point, the holding function, its deputy and the escalation route

text.en: List the decision points an AI system passes through from proposal to retirement.
Name the function holding each decision rather than the person doing it today.
Record the deputy who decides while the holding function is unavailable.
Set out where a decision goes when the holder cannot settle it.
Mark every decision point that no function currently claims.

title.en: Separate the function that clears an AI system for use from the one that builds it

description.en: Decide which approvals are reserved to a function outside the delivery team — releasing a system into live use, accepting a residual risk, overriding a monitoring threshold — and move them there in writing, with a reporting line that does not run back through the team whose work is being cleared. A reviewer who reports to the builder can only ever slow a release down, never stop one. Record what happens when the two disagree, because that is the case the structure exists for. Attach the terms of reference.

evidenceHint.en: Terms of reference for the clearing function: reserved approvals, reporting line and the disagreement route

text.en: Identify the approvals currently granted inside the team that builds the system.
Reserve each of those approvals to a function outside that team.
Set a reporting line that does not pass through the delivery team.
Write down what happens when the two functions disagree on a release.
Have the arrangement signed off by the body that owns the structure.

title.en: Open a confidential route for raising a concern about an AI system

description.en: Stand up the internal mechanism this control is really about: a way for anyone working with or around an AI system to report that it is behaving wrongly, being used beyond what was agreed, or harming someone — without needing the agreement of the team responsible for it. Offer at least one intake that does not require a name, say who reads what arrives and how quickly it is acknowledged, and state plainly what protection a person raising a concern has. A route nobody can find, or nobody believes is safe, produces the same silence as having none. Attach the description of the mechanism as it is published to staff.

evidenceHint.en: Published description of the concern mechanism: intake options, anonymity, acknowledgement time and the protection offered

text.en: Choose the intake routes, including one that carries no name.
Name who reads incoming concerns and how fast each is acknowledged.
State the protection from retaliation that a person raising a concern has.
Publish the route where people working near AI systems will meet it.
Walk a rehearsed concern through the route from intake to answer.

title.en: Log every concern raised about an AI system with its triage and outcome

description.en: Keep one record per concern carrying the date it arrived, the route it came in by, the system it names, the function it was routed to, what was decided and when it closed. Route from the accountability map rather than by judgement, so the same kind of concern does not reach a different desk each time. Record the outcome even where the answer was that nothing needed changing — the register is the only evidence that raising something leads anywhere, and a run of concerns closed with no action is itself a finding. Attach the register for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Concern register for the period: one row per submission with intake date, system, routing, decision and closure date

text.en: Record each concern with its arrival date and intake route.
Route it to the function the accountability map names for that system.
Record the decision reached and the date the concern closed.
Flag the concerns that changed how a system is built or run.

title.en: Sample recent AI decisions and confirm the accountable function actually took them

description.en: Draw a sample of decisions taken since the last review — releases, risk acceptances, changes to a live model — and find who actually took each one and under what authority, then read that against the map. Two failures show up only from this direction: a decision routinely taken by someone the map does not name, and a concern that travelled by a manager's inbox or a chat thread instead of the published route, which says the route is not trusted rather than not needed. Record each gap with the correction made to the structure. Attach the sample test.

evidenceHint.en: Sample test listing each decision examined, who took it, what the structure says, and every gap with its correction

text.en: Draw a sample of AI decisions taken since the last review.
Establish who took each one and on whose authority.
Compare that against the function the map holds accountable.
Look for concerns that travelled outside the published route.
Record each gap with the correction made to the structure.

templates.title: A.4 Resources for AI systems
templates.description: Implements AIMS-09: the datasets, models, algorithms, tooling, computing environments and people each AI system is built from are inventoried per system, kept current as they change, and reconciled against what is actually deployed.

title.en: Inventory the AI systems in scope and open a resource record for each

description.en: Resource control fails first on the systems nobody listed: a model built by one team, a vendor AI feature switched on inside a product, a fine-tune running in a research account. Work outwards from the AIMS scope boundary and from the places AI actually enters the organisation, and open one record per system carrying its owner, its purpose and a stable identifier that the dataset, model, environment and competence entries can all point back to. Settle here which resource classes every record must declare and which events oblige an owner to update it, because a register that is true only on the day it was built evidences nothing later.

evidenceHint.en: Register of AI systems in the AIMS scope, each with an owner, a stable identifier and the resource classes its record must declare

text.en: List every AI system inside the AIMS scope boundary, vendor-supplied features included.
Give each system a stable identifier and one named accountable owner.
Set the resource classes every record must declare: data, models and tooling, compute, people.
Name the events that oblige an owner to update a record, such as retraining or migration.
Publish the register where both system owners and auditors can reach it.

title.en: Catalogue the datasets each AI system depends on, with their source and terms of use

description.en: Capture what makes a dataset a resource rather than how it is handled: where it came from, who supplied or generated it, the licence, contract or consent basis permitting this particular use, where the copy the system actually reads is stored, and which systems consume it. Quality criteria, preparation and lineage belong to the data-management control and are not restated here. The failure this prevents is the dataset nobody can account for, a scraped corpus, a customer extract copied into a notebook, or a vendor sample whose evaluation licence lapsed, surfacing only when someone asks what the model was trained on.
